headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: CrewAI’s shared workspace and broad egress can feed gpt-researcher’s API-backed research pipeline.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and uses shared memory by default, while gpt-researcher reads local documents and can call MCP/API tools. That creates a plausible file-based or tool-output injection path if one agent consumes the other’s artifacts as instructions. The pair is not documented as isolated, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF CrewAI writes prompts or task files into a directory gpt-researcher later parses as instructions
IF gpt-researcher ingests CrewAI-generated reports without provenance filtering
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable automatic parsing of peer-generated files
Add a provenance tag to every handoff artifact
Review any shared MCP or API tool outputs before reuse

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and read local files; CrewAI explicitly handles API keys and crew-passed data, while gpt-researcher processes local documents and multiple external APIs. In a shared workspace, sensitive inputs can flow from one agent into the other’s outputs or outbound requests. This is a default-pathway risk, though not enough evidence for high.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same working directory
IF either agent sends file contents to its model or search APIs
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Use separate API keys per agent
Mount read-only input folders
Redact sensitive files before research runs
Log outbound requests for manual review

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; gpt-researcher can also read files, spawn subprocesses, and install packages. Even without explicit git overlap, they can contend over the same mutable workspace or generated artifacts. The profiles do not show locking or isolation, so a write-conflict pathway exists in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory
IF one agent overwrites files the other is still using
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Make shared inputs read-only
Run one agent at a time for mutable tasks

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI’s role-playing crews can emit synthesized outputs, and gpt-researcher’s planner/execution/publisher pipeline is designed to turn research into reports. If gpt-researcher treats CrewAI output as authoritative, errors or fabricated facts can cascade into published deliverables or downstream actions. Because this is a default workflow risk and verification is not shown, severity is high.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher uses CrewAI output as source material without independent verification
IF the publisher step forwards unreviewed claims into a report
mitigations: Require source citations for every claim
Insert a human review step before publishing
Compare CrewAI outputs against primary sources
Reject uncited or low-confidence statements

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, while gpt-researcher processes local documents, citations, and images through third-party APIs. If regulated or residency-bound data is placed into the pair, the mixed vendor/API path can create retention or jurisdiction mismatches. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF EU PII or regulated documents are sent through external APIs
IF the two agents have different retention or residency settings
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of external APIs
Use region-locked API endpoints
Document retention settings for both agents
Delete temporary research artifacts after use
